# Align the multi-window post with its Medium publication

## Context

The multi-window post went live on Medium on 2026-10-12: https://tobiasuhlig.medium.com/multi-window-web-apps-without-syncing-state-4b57e2b6722b

For readers who have never heard of Neo.mjs, the operator and I changed its opening there:
- **Title:** "Multi-window web apps without syncing state". The old title, "A web app that lives outside its windows.", doesn't say which windows, and names neither the problem nor the benefit.
- **Subtitle:** capability first.
- **Disclosure:** one sentence, kept within the first two paragraphs as Medium's AI content policy asks.
- **Cover caption:** labels the cover an AI-generated illustration, as that policy also asks. Emmy generated the cover with an image model (pages#28; her receipt calls it a marketing illustration).

At least one large subreddit refuses Medium links, so its submission will point at the post on GitHub. That copy still opens with the old title, the old byline and an unlabeled AI cover. Verified: `learn/blog/a-workspace-that-can-leave-its-window.md` and `apps/portal/resources/data/blog.json` at `origin/dev` `809f9ff49c` are the only places carrying the old title.

## The Fix

Mirror the published Medium wording into the GitHub copy:
1. `learn/blog/a-workspace-that-can-leave-its-window.md`
   - H1: "Multi-window web apps without syncing state".
   - The bold lede becomes the Medium subtitle.
   - The byline becomes the Medium disclosure: written by Grace, edited by Tobias Uhlig, reviewed by a second AI model family.
   - The cover's alt text, plus an italic caption in the post's existing caption style, says it is an AI-generated illustration and that the film is a real capture.
2. `apps/portal/resources/data/blog.json`: this entry's `name` equals the new H1, following the convention from #19639.

The file name and route (`blog/a-workspace-that-can-leave-its-window`) stay as they are, so existing links keep working.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The H1, lede, disclosure line and cover caption match the live Medium post's text. Character-level differences are allowed only where Markdown links replace Medium's.
- [ ] The `blog.json` `name` equals the H1. No other entry changes.
- [ ] GitHub renders the post: both Mermaid diagrams, the cover, and the film link.

## Out of Scope

- neomjs.com: the Portal picks this up with the next release, or through a separate Pages publication if one is wanted.
- The post's body below the opening, which Medium carries unchanged.
